draft.title: Organelles and their jobs
card: Organelles are small structures inside a cell. Each one does a particular job, so the cell can carry out many tasks at once.
Nucleus
holds the cell's DNA, which contains the instructions for making proteins.
Mitochondria
release energy from glucose in a form the cell can use, called ATP. Ribosomes make proteins by joining amino acids together.
Chloroplasts
carry out photosynthesis, which uses light energy to make glucose. They are found in plant cells and some other organisms, such as algae.
draft.remember: Nucleus: DNA. Mitochondria: energy release. Ribosomes: proteins. Chloroplasts: photosynthesis.

a.q: A cell is making large amounts of protein. Which organelle is directly joining amino acids together?
a.why: Ribosomes join amino acids to make proteins. The nucleus holds the DNA instructions, but it does not assemble the protein itself.
a.clue: Which organelle does the building, not the storing of instructions?

b.q: Muscle cells in a sprinter use ATP very quickly. Which organelle would these cells have in unusually large numbers?
b.why: Mitochondria release energy as ATP, so a cell with a high energy demand needs many of them. Ribosomes make proteins, which is a different job, and muscle cells do not carry out photosynthesis.
b.clue: Which organelle releases the energy the cell uses?

problems.detail: The sprinter is a poor example. Sprinting relies mostly on fast-twitch fibres and anaerobic ATP supply, and these fibres have relatively few mitochondria. Endurance (slow-twitch) muscle fibres are the ones with unusually many mitochondria. Use an endurance athlete, or heart muscle cells, instead.

Skeletal muscle fibres really do contain unusually many nuclei, because they are multinucleate. Taken literally, 'Which organelle would these cells have in unusually large numbers?' therefore has a second true answer, 'Nuclei'. Tie the stem explicitly to supplying ATP.

check.summary: Question b uses a sprinter, but sprint (fast-twitch) muscle fibres are relatively low in mitochondria, so an endurance athlete or heart muscle would be accurate. The stem could also be read as allowing 'Nuclei', since skeletal muscle fibres are multinucleate.

b.q: Heart muscle cells contract nonstop and need a steady supply of ATP. Which organelle supplies this ATP, so it is found in large numbers?
b.why: Mitochondria release energy from glucose as ATP, so cells with a constant energy demand have many of them. Ribosomes make proteins and the nucleus holds DNA, so neither supplies ATP. Heart cells do not photosynthesise, so they have no chloroplasts.
b.clue: Which organelle releases energy in a form the cell can use?
